basis_note: today's members applied to the past; not point-in-time; survivors only
no_outcomes: series only: no outcome relation, no regime assignment, no trading call of any kind, on any period
scope: series only: group and universe numbers; no member ticker, row or price; no regime assignment of any kind

start.rule: first January 1 from which every later calendar year has name-week above-200 flag disagreement against the Tiingo archive of 0.5% or less (S&P 500 members priced in both, weeks where both hold 200 sessions)
start.note: 200-session averages use the full download, so the first weeks after the start read flags from late in the prior year

index.rebalance_rule: engine.baskets._ew_level: each session the index return is the plain mean of the daily total returns of the members priced that session (daily rebalance to equal weight), chained from 1.0 on the group's first valid session
index.floor_gap: On a session with fewer than 2 priced members the level is missing (reason below_index_member_floor) and that session carries no return; the chain resumes from the last valid level.
index.dividend_effect: A difference in dividend method shifts the long-run level of a total-return index, not the timing of its turns.
index.survivors_only_effect: The index holds only names alive today, so its past returns are overstated, more so the further back and in themes with high failure rates; relative turns between groups are less affected than levels, and that is not tested here.

high_beta_computed.rule: top fifth of universe members by trailing 252-session beta to SPY daily returns (cov/var on 252 paired daily returns, full window required), ranked at each month's last session, held the next month; ties broken by ticker; equal-weight daily rebalance within the held month, same _ew_level chaining from 1.0

price_source: yfinance yf.download(auto_adjust=True, period='max'), one single-vintage download, held off git; never the collector cache or data/yahoo

price_topup.call: yf.download(<one ticker>, period='max', auto_adjust=True), one call per ticker
price_topup.rule: each name's full history is from a single download; no ticker has history from two downloads (COO 2026-11-12 09:39Z)
price_topup.reason: members of the relationship-hub families absent from the first download

etf_source: data/yahoo/<T>.parquet on origin/main, column close (vendor price series, not the house auto_adjust download); read with git show, never edited

universe.basis: today's S&P 500 members and today's GICS sector labels, same family sector basis as scripts/build_tree_breadth_and_index.py

house_history_check.question: does the house breadth history already hold universe rows?
house_history_check.answer: no universe group exists in any house history file; every universe breadth series here is new
house_history_check.live_surface_note: data/breadth/breadth.parquet (the live nightly collector surface) does carry universe pct_above_50/200 and nh/nl, but on collector-cache prices, not the house download; it is not history and is not mixed into this house-basis file
house_history_check.source_rule: These series sit on a different price source from the sector breadth history (group_breadth_*_current.parquet, Tiingo archive); the two are never joined or mixed.

weights_check.question: are historical S&P 500 index weights on main?
weights_check.answer: no: constituents files hold today's members only (name, sector), desk_weights/shadow.json is desk allocation, rate_futures constituents are futures contracts, cpi_relative_importance is CPI weights
weights_check.decision: count-based leadership only; the weight-based top-10 measure is skipped
